attachments.origin_landmark: 2nd, 4th, and 5th metacarpal shafts (single-headed, unlike the dorsal group)

actions: adduct fingers toward the axial line (digit 3)

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: 3 separate small unipennate muscles (TA: interossei palmares I-III), unlike the dorsal interossei's bipennate 2-metacarpal origin -- there is no palmar interosseous for digit 3 itself, since it is the reference axis both groups act relative to.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the dorsum of the hand, 1-2 cm proximal to the metacarpophalangeal joints, aiming deep to the dorsal interossei.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Three muscles lying deeper than the dorsal interossei, between the cortices of metacarpals II-V.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Usually injected together with the lumbricals and dorsal interossei when the intrinsic-plus pattern is being treated.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

trigger_points.location_description: PI-1 (first palmar interosseous): palpated through the palm against the 2nd metacarpal shaft, or dorsally alongside the first dorsal interosseous of the same interspace; the deep arch and deep ulnar branch cross the field proximally.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Refers along the ulnar side of the index finger, with deep hand ache -- the same rule as the dorsal group: pain along the attached side of the corresponding finger.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forceful adduction-pinch (holding charts/tablets, cards, syringes between fingers), prolonged writing.
trigger_points.notes: The Heberden-node association applies to the interossei as a group and is hypothesis-level, not established causation.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1, Ch. 40, pp. 786-793 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document

trigger_points.location_description: PI-2 (second palmar interosseous): palpated through the palm against the 4th metacarpal shaft, or dorsally alongside the corresponding dorsal interosseous of the same interspace; the deep arch and deep ulnar branch cross the field proximally.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Refers along the radial side of the ring finger, with deep hand ache -- the same rule as the dorsal group: pain along the attached side of the corresponding finger.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forceful adduction-pinch (holding charts/tablets, cards, syringes between fingers), prolonged writing.
trigger_points.notes: The Heberden-node association applies to the interossei as a group and is hypothesis-level, not established causation.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1, Ch. 40, pp. 786-793 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document

trigger_points.location_description: PI-3 (third palmar interosseous): palpated through the palm against the 5th metacarpal shaft, or dorsally alongside the corresponding dorsal interosseous of the same interspace; the deep arch and deep ulnar branch cross the field proximally.
trigger_points.referred_pain_pattern: Refers along the radial side of the little finger, with deep hand ache -- the same rule as the dorsal group: pain along the attached side of the corresponding finger; for the little-finger side this overlaps the ulnar-hand referral list under abductor digiti minimi.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Forceful adduction-pinch (holding charts/tablets, cards, syringes between fingers), prolonged writing.
trigger_points.notes: The Heberden-node association applies to the interossei as a group and is hypothesis-level, not established causation. Loss of PI-3 produces the Wartenberg sign (D5 drifts into abduction under unopposed EDM).
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual, Vol. 1, Ch. 40, pp. 786-793 -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded hand intrinsic muscle reference document
